A1.justification: Both complete 25-page PDFs describe the same research work. Text and rendered-page inspection covers the equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-H, with no material gaps preventing comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, adapter ablations and efficiency analyses in Section 5, with additional empirical results in Appendices C-H.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains both Learnable Calibration variants, adapter merging, calibration objectives, parameter sharing and the inference procedure unchanged.

E1.justification: The same datasets, four compositional task families, languages and tones are retained. The SAMSum domain-shift evaluation and three-task compositions in Appendices E-F are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Table 2 and the corresponding appendix experiments, including TIES, DARE, LoraHub, LM-Cocktail, DAM/ZipLoRA, multi-step LoRA usage and joint-expert LoRA.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, model configurations, training budgets, ROUGE metrics, LLM-judge evaluation and task prompts are unchanged, including the protocols used for appendix experiments.

E4.justification: The parameter-sharing and pre-existing-adapter ablations, update-matrix analysis, scaling study, domain-shift tests, qualitative examples and learning-curve analysis are identical in both versions.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same averaging across models and languages or tones. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains Learnable Calibration++ scores of 28.64 ROUGE-L and 65.15 LLM-J for summarization plus translation; appendix results are also identical.

T1.justification: The compositional-task definition, assumptions and mathematical formulations in Equations 1-7 are unchanged. No theoretical results or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: compositional multi-tasking for on-device LLMs, a four-task benchmark and efficient Learnable Calibration methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations of calibration, efficiency, generalization and failure behaviors are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning model scale and the number of composed tasks.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendices A-B retain identical hyperparameters, training details, evaluation prompts and hyperparameter-selection information. The project-page disclosure and access link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The revised grammatical-error-correction reference retains the same five-author group, year and ACL venue. Its author/title metadata and corresponding citation change, without adding a distinct cited work or revising research positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction changes Severyn et al. (2021) to Rothe et al. (2021). The bibliography revises author order/name forms and changes the title from 'Grammatical error correction using large multilingual language models' to 'A simple recipe for multilingual grammatical error correction.' The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; other prose and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions, axes, legends and placements are unchanged, including the appendices. The localized citation and bibliography edits preserve the existing page layout.

improvement.justification: v3 is confined to a bibliographic metadata revision and its corresponding citation, plus version metadata. The scientific argument, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, limitations and appendix material remain identical, leaving overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
